name: Intel oneAPI DPC++/C++ Compiler (icpx)
workload: Runtime of a single-threaded equity-volatility quant pipeline (parse ~30M option quotes from a 1 GB pcap, Black-Scholes implied-vol Newton inversion, SVI smile fits, greeks) built with GCC, Clang and icpx from identical source in strict-IEEE and fast-math variants.
claimed_speedup: icpx-fast finishes the pipeline 1.79x faster than gcc-strict (13700 ms vs 24536 ms total) and 1.44x faster than the best non-Intel variant (clang-fast-zmm, 20453 ms). Under strict IEEE the field compresses to 1.00-1.23x (icpx-strict 19920 ms vs gcc-strict 24536 ms vs clang-strict 22475 ms). SVI fit stage 2385 ms vs 8879 ms (3.7x) and greeks 770 ms vs 2571 ms (3.3x) for icpx-fast vs gcc-strict.
compiler_and_flags: gcc 13.3.0 -O3 -march=native -funroll-loops [-ffast-math]; clang 18.1.8 -O3 -march=native [-ffast-math -fveclib=libmvec]; icpx (IntelLLVM 2025.3.3) -O3 -xHost -fp-model=precise (strict) or -fp-model=fast -fimf-precision=high (fast); zmm variants add -mprefer-vector-width=512 or -qopt-zmm-usage=high
hardware: 4-vCPU KVM guest on a 5th-gen Xeon Scalable (Emerald Rapids, family 6 model 207; hypervisor masks the retail SKU), AVX-512 exposed; shared cloud host, single session
license: Apache-2.0 (intel/llvm open-source base); the benchmarked icpx binary came from the proprietary oneapi-basekit image
stars_or_usage: intel/llvm 1.5k stars (open-source base of the oneAPI DPC++ compiler); benchmark repo yzia2000/qr_cpp_compiler 0 stars, 8 commits Aug 1-2 2026
tradeoffs: Most of the gain needs -fp-model=fast (relaxed floating point) and Intel's SVML/libimf vector math; Intel hardware oriented (-xHost); closed-source optimizer components in the shipped product; proprietary terms for the shipped binary.
caveats: Benchmark is a small personal repo (0 stars, no LICENSE file seen, 8 commits in two days) on a transcendental-heavy workload chosen to favour SVML; it is a single session on a shared cloud VM so numbers are relative; CPU SKU is masked (family 6 model 207 stated), so tier A is borderline. The README itself notes gcc-fast beats icpx-fast on the Newton IV stage (3.07 vs 2.83 Mq/s), strict-IEEE advantage is only 1.23x, and forcing 512-bit vectors made icpx 14.8% slower. Corroboration, opened: LAMMPS issue #5213 (author akohlmey, Sept 2026, 2x20-core Xeon Gold 6248 Cascade Lake, RHEL 10, GCC 14 -O3 -march=native -ffast-math vs icpx 2026.1 -xHost -fp-model fast=2, values relative to GCC 14 '-sf intel') reports icpx at lj 1.70, rhodo 1.62, sw 1.85, water 1.88, airebo 1.85, tersoff 1.49, snap 3.48, but lc 0.91 and dpd 1.02, so it is not uniformly faster. Counter-evidence, opened: gist kaityo256/d41481467df504c5039715d38954ab8a (GCC 5.4-9.2 vs ICC 18-19.1 vs Clang 8, -O3 -march=native/-xHOST, four Intel CPUs) shows GCC 40-60x faster on a degenerate std::uniform_real_distribution loop (0.05s vs 2.72s on Xeon Gold 6230). Search-snippet only (pages blocked here, not opened): SPEC withdrew over 2,000 SPEC CPU 2017 results that used a benchmark-specific oneAPI DPC++ optimization, and older ICC-vs-GCC articles show the gap narrowing. The listed 'Intel C++ Compiler' (software.intel.com) is the proprietary product; repo_url points at its open-source base, which is not what was benchmarked.

name: LLVM lld (LLVM linker)
workload: Link time of four large debug-info programs (ffmpeg, mysqld, clang, chromium) with GNU ld, GNU gold and lld, each with and without multi-threading.
claimed_speedup: lld w/threads vs GNU gold w/threads: ffmpeg dbg 0.35s vs 1.01s, mysqld dbg 0.68s vs 2.68s, clang dbg 5.28s vs 23.49s, chromium dbg 16.70s vs 60.82s; GNU ld took 1.72s, 8.50s, 104.03s and 209.05s on the same four programs. Docs text: 'you can expect that LLD runs more than twice as fast as the GNU gold linker' on a large program on a multicore machine.
hardware: 2-socket 20-core 40-thread Xeon E5-2680 2.80 GHz machine with an SSD drive
tradeoffs: Drop-in replacement for GNU linkers (same command line and linker scripts); ELF, PE/COFF, Mach-O and WebAssembly ports of differing completeness; LTO supported by default; some very old Unix linker features removed.
caveats: First-party table in the lld docs, undated but from about 2017 (the same page says 'as of February 2017'); the four programs, link command lines, compiler and flags are not given, so it cannot be reproduced from the page; hardware is stated. GNU ld rows drop -icf=all and -gdb-index because GNU ld lacks them (footnote says GNU ld would be slower with them). The docs warn results vary with cores, memory and disk. Newer linkers such as mold are faster than lld. llvm-project is already in the catalog (AddressSanitizer entry), so this lld record needs a distinct id or paper: key before merge. The 'LLVM' list entry is a collection; lld is the component with the clearest numeric comparison found. A numeric Clang-vs-GCC compile-time comparison was not found on a reachable page (blog.llvm.org blocked).

name: Microsoft Visual C++ (MSVC cl.exe)
workload: Building Node.js on Windows with vcbuild.bat using MSVC versus vcbuild.bat clang-cl.
claimed_speedup: 'ClangCL compilation is ~2.5 slower (less with x64, more with ARM64)' than MSVC, i.e. MSVC compiles about 2.5x faster (inverse derived from page data).
stars_or_usage: Standard Windows C++ toolchain; evidence is a Node.js build issue (Oct 1, 2024)
tradeoffs: Proprietary closed-source compiler (the open part is MSVC STL, microsoft/STL, not benchmarked here); Windows-oriented; in the numeric runtime comparisons found MSVC-generated code was often slower than clang-cl or GCC.
caveats: Single issue report by a Node.js contributor with no hardware, compiler versions, flags or raw timings; the stated cause is that MSVC uses precompiled headers and clang-cl did not, and the issue was closed by Node.js PR #55249 which enables PCH for clang-cl ('improves ClangCL compilation time drastically'), so the gap is obsolete. MSVC is a closed binary, so there is no repo; usability set to reference. Opened counter-evidence on generated-code speed: simdjson issue #847 (MSVC 19.25.28614 overall 1.3051 vs ClangCL 9.0.0 2.2221 on twitter.json, Haswell, Release) and issue #812 show MSVC slower than ClangCL and g++. Weak extra compile-time data, opened: vcpkg issue #15961 (about 36 s MSVC on Windows vs about 1 min 10 s GCC on Ubuntu under WSL, different platforms, no versions or flags). Search-snippet only (pages blocked, not opened): Chrome team post says building Chrome locally with Clang is about 15% slower than MSVC. The docs.microsoft.com URL in the list is a C++/CLI page with no performance data; Microsoft's devblogs and learn.microsoft.com were blocked.
